title: Teaching Elders Byron Snapp and James M. Hope v. Calvary Presbytery
disposition_detail: The Assembly adopted the commission’s judgment sustaining the complaint’s single specification, finding the ordination contrary to the Book of Church Order, and remanding the matter to Calvary Presbytery for correction. It separately directed preparation of a report to the Ninth General Assembly on the proper use of the extraordinary clause.
first_summary: Teaching Elders challenged Calvary Presbytery’s use of the extraordinary clause to examine and ordain a candidate who had completed only one quarter of Hebrew. The commission sustained the complaint because Presbytery had not demonstrated extraordinary circumstances or the candidate’s proven extraordinary gifts. It found the ordination contrary to the Book of Church Order and remanded for correction. The broader question concerning proper use of the clause was assigned for a report to the next Assembly.
summary: Teaching Elders challenged Calvary Presbytery’s use of the extraordinary clause to examine and ordain a candidate who had completed only one quarter of Hebrew. The Assembly sustained the complaint’s single specification because Presbytery had not demonstrated either extraordinary circumstances or the man’s proven extraordinary gifts. It found the ordination contrary to the Book of Church Order and remanded for correction. Rather than answer the broader question about proper use of the clause, it ordered a report to the Ninth General Assembly.
